## Library Clusters {#extension-areas .section-title}

```{=html}
<div class="section-card-grid">
  <article class="section-card">
    <span class="section-eyebrow">Observation</span>
    <h3>Remote Sensing Library</h3>
    <p>Orbits, GPS, sensing geometry, radar, LiDAR, thermal methods, gravity, and retrieval logic form a coherent observation branch.</p>
    <p><a href="../advanced-remote-sensing/">Advanced Remote Sensing</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="section-card">
    <span class="section-eyebrow">Cold Systems</span>
    <h3>Cryosphere and Mountain Systems</h3>
    <p>Snow, glaciers, permafrost, alpine hydrology, and mountain hazards form a distinct field-focused branch of the project.</p>
    <p><a href="../cryosphere-and-mountain-systems/">Cryosphere and Mountain Systems</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="section-card">
    <span class="section-eyebrow">Human Systems</span>
    <h3>Economic Geography and Infrastructure</h3>
    <p>Trade, transport, pipelines, pricing, and energy systems belong together as a strong human-systems branch beyond the gateway chapters in the core book.</p>
    <p><a href="../economic-systems/">Economic Systems</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="section-card">
    <span class="section-eyebrow">Methods</span>
    <h3>Machine Learning and Inference</h3>
    <p>Open these later, once the logic of modelling, uncertainty, and spatial analysis already feels familiar.</p>
    <p><a href="../machine-learning/">Machine Learning</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="section-card">
    <span class="section-eyebrow">Observation Support</span>
    <h3>Orbits, GPS, and Sensing Geometry</h3>
    <p>Some Earth observation foundations still live inside Environmental Systems for now, but they function as part of the wider remote sensing library.</p>
    <p><a href="../environmental-systems/">Environmental Systems</a></p>
  </article>
</div>
```
